concepts.name: Federal Structure and All-India Federation Proposal
key_dimensions: Distinction between the proposed federation and actual British Indian provinces vs. princely states joining voluntarily
Why the federation never came into existence — instrument of accession threshold not met (50% princely states + half their population required)
Comparison with the federation that actually came into force in 1950 Constitution
UPSC trap: Federal Part of the Act never implemented, only Provincial Part was operationalized in 1937

concepts.name: Division of Powers: Federal, Provincial, and Concurrent Lists
key_dimensions: Three-fold division into Federal List (59 subjects), Provincial List (54 subjects), and Concurrent List (36 subjects) — precursor to Indian Constitution's Seventh Schedule
Residuary powers vested in Governor-General, not Parliament — contrast with Indian Constitution where residuary powers go to Union
Supremacy of Federal Legislature in case of conflict in Concurrent List subjects
UPSC trap: Residuary powers placement differs from the 1950 Constitution — a common comparison question

concepts.name: Provincial Autonomy: Nature, Scope, and Limitations
key_dimensions: Provincial Autonomy as the most significant operative feature — introduced in 1937 under Part II of the Act
Governors retained special/reserve powers and 'individual judgment' powers that curtailed real autonomy
Distinction between 'constitutional discretion' and 'individual judgment' of Governors
UPSC trap: Provincial autonomy was 'real but limited' — questions often probe whether it was genuine or a facade due to Governor's overriding powers

concepts.name: Governor's Powers: Discretion, Special Responsibilities, and Individual Judgment
key_dimensions: Three categories: Acts in 'individual judgment' (no ministerial advice needed), 'special responsibilities' (consult ministers but can override), and normal constitutional functions
Special responsibilities included prevention of grave menace to peace, protection of minorities, safeguarding British commercial interests
Comparison with post-1950 Governor's role — Article 163 vs. Governor's sweeping 1935 powers
UPSC trap: Difference between 'discretion,' 'individual judgment,' and 'special responsibilities' — three distinct legal concepts often conflated

concepts.name: Governor-General's Position and Viceregal Powers
key_dimensions: Governor-General acted as Crown's representative and had overriding powers over the Federal Legislature
Power to issue Governor-General's Acts when legislature was not in session or refused to pass a bill
Certification powers — could certify a bill as essential for safety/tranquility even if rejected by legislature
UPSC trap: Governor-General retained full control over Defence, Foreign Affairs, and Ecclesiastical matters — not subject to Federal Executive Council

concepts.name: Federal Court: Jurisdiction, Composition, and Significance
key_dimensions: Established in 1937 — first apex judicial body in India with original, appellate, and advisory jurisdiction
Original jurisdiction: disputes between federation and units or inter-unit disputes (not available to individuals)
Appeals lay to the Privy Council in London, not the Federal Court — limitation on judicial sovereignty
UPSC trap: Federal Court ≠ Supreme Court of India; Privy Council remained the final appellate body — a key distinction

concepts.name: Bicameral Legislature at Centre: Council of State and Federal Assembly
key_dimensions: Council of State (Upper House): 260 members, partly elected by provinces, partly nominated by princely states — 6-year term, permanent body
Federal Assembly (Lower House): 375 members, indirect election — 5-year term
Since Federation never materialized, the Central Legislature under 1919 Act continued to function
UPSC trap: Federal Legislature never came into existence — questions test whether candidates know only the Provincial Legislature (1937) was operationalized

concepts.name: Dyarchy: Abolition at Provinces, Introduction at Centre
key_dimensions: Dyarchy abolished at provincial level (introduced by Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms 1919) — full responsible government introduced in provinces
Dyarchy introduced at the Centre for the first time — federal subjects divided into Reserved (under Governor-General) and Transferred (under Executive Council)
Reserved subjects at Centre: Defence, External Affairs, Ecclesiastical Affairs, Tribal Areas
UPSC trap: 1935 Act reversed the dyarchy arrangement — abolished where it existed (provinces) and introduced where it didn't (Centre)

concepts.name: Communal Representation and Separate Electorates
key_dimensions: Extended and entrenched the system of separate electorates for Muslims, Sikhs, Europeans, Anglo-Indians, and Indian Christians
Poona Pact (1932) context — Scheduled Castes got reserved seats in general electorates (joint electorates with reserved seats, not separate electorates)
Franchise extended but still limited — about 14% of population (from 3% under 1919 Act)
UPSC trap: Scheduled Castes did NOT get separate electorates under 1935 Act — they got reserved seats in joint electorates, contrast with other communities

concepts.name: Instrument of Accession and Princely States' Integration Mechanism
key_dimensions: Princely states could join the federation by executing an Instrument of Accession — voluntary, not compulsory
Accession could be limited to specific subjects — states could negotiate terms unlike British Indian provinces
Threshold for federation: States representing 50% of the total population and 52 of 104 Chamber of Princes seats had to accede
UPSC trap: This mechanism was the direct precursor to post-1947 Instrument of Accession used to integrate princely states — continuity of legal concept

concepts.name: Council of India: Abolition and Its Significance
key_dimensions: Council of India (established by Government of India Act 1858) was abolished by the 1935 Act
Secretary of State's advisory council replaced — Secretary of State could now act more independently but was aided by advisors
Symbolized reduced direct control of India Office over Indian administration
UPSC trap: Abolition of Council of India ≠ abolition of Secretary of State — Secretary of State continued with modified powers

concepts.name: Reserve Bank of India: Establishment under the Act
key_dimensions: RBI established in 1935 under provisions of the Government of India Act 1935
Originally a private shareholders' bank — nationalized only in 1949
Separation of currency and credit management from the government's direct control
UPSC trap: RBI's establishment is often tested as a provision of the 1935 Act — candidates must link constitutional development to institutional creation

concepts.name: Federal Public Service Commission and Provincial Public Services
key_dimensions: Establishment of Federal Public Service Commission (FPSC) and Provincial Public Service Commissions — statutory bodies for the first time
Joint Public Service Commissions possible for two or more provinces
Precursor to UPSC and State PSCs under the 1950 Constitution — Articles 315–323
UPSC trap: The 1935 Act made PSCs statutory (legally mandated) for the first time, not just advisory bodies

concepts.name: Franchise and Electoral Provisions: Expansion and Limitations
key_dimensions: Electorate expanded from ~7 million (1919 Act) to ~35 million — still property/tax/literacy based qualification
Women's franchise included on the same basis as men — significant step though still limited
No universal adult franchise — contrast with 1950 Constitution's Article 326 which introduced universal adult suffrage
UPSC trap: 1935 Act is often falsely credited with introducing universal suffrage — it only expanded limited franchise to ~14% of population

concepts.name: Indian Congress's Response and 1937 Provincial Elections
key_dimensions: Congress initially rejected the Act as 'fundamentally bad' and a 'new charter of slavery' — Nehru called it a 'machine with strong brakes but no engine'
Despite opposition, Congress contested 1937 elections and won majorities in 6 of 11 provinces
Congress ministries resigned in 1939 following India being declared a party to WWII without consultation
UPSC trap: Congress boycotted the Joint Select Committee deliberations but participated in elections — apparent contradiction tested in analysis questions

concepts.name: Simon Commission and Round Table Conferences as Precursors
key_dimensions: Simon Commission (1927–1930): No Indian member — boycotted by all Indian parties; its report formed the basis of the 1935 Act
Three Round Table Conferences (1930–1932) — Congress absent in 1st, participated in 2nd (Gandhi), absent in 3rd
White Paper (1933) → Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC) → Government of India Act 1935
UPSC trap: Simon Commission report ≠ 1935 Act directly; the White Paper and JPC were intermediate steps — sequencing errors are commonly tested

concepts.name: Relationship between the 1935 Act and the Indian Constitution of 1950
key_dimensions: Many provisions of the Indian Constitution borrowed directly: Federal structure, distribution of powers, Emergency provisions, Public Service Commissions, Federal Court → Supreme Court
Ambedkar acknowledged the structural borrowings but emphasized the 1950 Constitution's democratic spirit vs. 1935 Act's colonial control
Critical differences: No fundamental rights in 1935 Act, no Directive Principles, no sovereign democratic republic character
UPSC trap: Questions ask 'which features were NOT borrowed' — Fundamental Rights, Directive Principles, and Preamble were original additions, not derived from 1935

concepts.name: Emergency Powers and Central Control over Provinces
key_dimensions: Governor-General could suspend provincial autonomy and assume direct control — precursor to President's Rule under Article 356
Proclamation of emergency could override the entire federal-provincial division of powers
Governor's power to dissolve provincial assembly and impose Governor's Rule within provinces

UPSC trap: The 1935 Act's emergency provisions were the direct template for Articles 352, 356, and 360 — but with key difference: 1935 provisions were unilateral executive acts, not parliamentary acts

concepts.name: Burma's Separation from India under the 1935 Act
key_dimensions: Burma formally separated from India by the Government of Burma Act 1935 (companion legislation)
Burma had been part of British India since 1886 — separation effective April 1, 1937
Aden also separated from India in 1937 — both under the broader reorganization accompanying the 1935 Act
UPSC trap: Separation of Burma is sometimes tested as a provision 'within' the 1935 Act — it was a separate but simultaneous legislation; candidates must distinguish

concepts.name: Sindh and Orissa: Creation of New Provinces
key_dimensions: Sindh carved out of Bombay Presidency — became a separate Governor's Province under the 1935 Act (effective 1936)
Orissa carved out of Bihar and Orissa Province — became a separate province on the basis of linguistic identity
North-West Frontier Province elevated from Chief Commissioner's Province to Governor's Province with full legislative council
UPSC trap: The reorganization of 1935 Act created new provinces on administrative/communal lines — contrast with post-1956 States Reorganization Act based on linguistic lines
